commits.message:
fix(pretty): a value from another realm prints as the same value made here (rich-pretty-dzzp)

describesItself compared toString against this realm's Object.prototype.toString,
and formOf/indexedElements classified Map, Set and DataView with instanceof, so
a vm-context or iframe object printed [object Object], [object Map], or (for a
DataView) an empty array. Every classification now asks the value's internal
slot through a borrowed built-in brand check, and the default-toString test
compares against the Object.prototype of the value's own realm.

The Map/Set bound tests faked a collection by grafting Set.prototype onto a
plain object; they now use real subclasses, which the brand check accepts.

fix(highlighter)!: ReprHighlighter and the repr.* styles draw what Rich draws (rich-highlighter-nct1) (#309)

* fix(highlighter): ReprHighlighter and the repr.* styles draw what Rich draws (rich-highlighter-nct1)

ReprHighlighter now carries Rich 15.0.0's patterns, compiled for the u flag
with Python's Unicode \w, \b and \d spelled out, and DEFAULT_STYLES carries
Rich's repr.* table. RegexHighlighter places each group by its match index
(the d flag) instead of searching the match for the group's text, which found
the first copy rather than the captured one.

test/core/repr-highlight.golden.json is Rich's own spans and truecolor bytes
for every string in Rich's highlight_tests plus the ticket's repro; its test
header carries the command that regenerates it. Kept divergence: JavaScript's
true/false/null/undefined are styled like True/False/None, for Pretty.

* test(highlighter): generate the Rich golden at print's defaults, as the port prints it (rich-highlighter-nct1)
